newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens weaker on soft overseas trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens weaker on soft overseas trade.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened weaker at C$1.3928 (US$0.7179) in light trading on Wednesday after the unit traded in a narrow, easier range last night on overseas markets, trader said. * They said rumors that Japanese institutional investors may decide to redeem large amounts of Canadian bonds at the end of the month had a minimal impact on the Canadian dollar.

"It is worth noting that many of these issues will trade as money market instruments once they have less than a year to maturity, so it may well be that a lot of this (cash) is already back in domestic money market account portfolios," one trader said.
Analysts said the Canadian dollar was likely to continue trading in a weak range as speculation that the U.S. Federal Reserve might raise interest rates next week snowballed.
The Federal Open Market Committee will meet on July 1-2 to decide whether the U.S. economy is growing fast enough to warrant a rate hike.
The Conference Board, a private U.S. business research group, reported on Tuesday that its index of consumer confidence rose to 129.6 for June, the highest reading since 1969.
Economists said the robust U.S. economic growth set the stage for some Fed tightening in late summer or early fall, which would place added pressure on the Canadian dollar.

"There was a little reprieve for the Canada (dollar) in the last couple of weeks because indicators were coming out in the U.S. a little on the soft side," said John Anania, economist with the Royal Bank of Canada.
But Anania said that stronger-than-expected U.S. growth in the third quarter could surprise the markets and force the Canadian dollar into a downdraft.
Overseas, the Japanese yen strengthened after Japan's quarterly Tankan survey of business sentiment reported that the manufacturing index rose a bullish 7.0 percent since the last survey in March.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar dropped to 81.52 yen from Tuesday's close of 82.51 yen and dipped to 1.2371 marks from Tuesday's 1.2396 marks.
